correctness.rationale: For each 0<beta<1, the six-term H generalized polynomial has four coefficient sign changes and a double root at q=1. Its strict opposing endpoint signs force exactly one simple zero in (0,1). Direct derivation of the mandatory innovation PGF shows R_c'(0)/R_c(0)=-(1-c)H/(1-q)^2+O((1-c)^2); thus above the sharp root all sufficiently high retentions are impossible. Uniform Taylor expansions establish both endpoint constants. A positive stable mixture and log-convex renewal proof independently supply ordinary ID. Decimal recomputation and package checker passed. No infinite claim rests solely on enumeration.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The prior result says that for every positive integer m the count law is the m-fold ordinary convolution of iid count laws. The present failure says that an independent innovation cannot complete a binomial-thinned copy of X for high retention. Neither assertion implies the other. Previous general INAR discussions define the property but do not state this discrete Weibull q_*(beta) criterion in materials read.

The standard discrete self-decomposability condition is the existence of a probability generating quotient at every Bernoulli retention; the present theorem derives an explicit negative one-count quotient coefficient and an exact zero curve.

The new root is not a parameter rename of the pre-existing ID classification.

value.rationale: The uniquely defined obstruction curve answers an operationally natural question left open by the ordinary-ID classification: which parameters of the established discrete Weibull family are excluded as stationary marginals of binomial-thinning autoregressions with high retention. It gives an all-shape exact necessary exclusion and sharp two-limit scaling, not an arbitrary slice or isolated negative example. It also demonstrates model-specifically why standard additive infinite divisibility is insufficient. The result deliberately does not claim a complete stationarity region.
